persona: Owner or service head of a distributor selling and maintaining industrial machinery for manufacturing plants

sections.h2: What changes when the customer is a factory
paras: An industrial equipment distributor sells into plants, and a plant does not measure a fault in inconvenience. It measures it in stopped production. That single fact reorders the software requirement: the asset has to be findable by plant and by line, the call has to be timestamped and answered against a promise, the engineer has to arrive with the right part, and the whole thing has to be evidenced afterwards because the customer's maintenance head reports on it.

Around the breakdown sits ordinary distribution work: quotations to a purchase department, machines supplied and commissioned, annual contracts, planned maintenance scheduled into the plant's shutdown windows, and a spares business that is often larger than the machine business. Aura Business holds all of it on one platform with a mobile app for engineers who work in places with no network.

sections.h2: The call comes at six in the morning and the line is stopped.
sections.lead: Industrial customers are unforgiving about response and indifferent to excuses about paperwork.

items.p: The caller says a pump in the packing hall. Without a plant-wise register, identifying the machine is the first half hour.

items.h: The engineer arrives without the part
items.p: The fault could have been guessed from the service history, but the history is in an old job book.
The plant has shutdown windows twice a year, and your preventive visits are not scheduled against them.
Gate entry, safety induction and work permits are arranged on arrival rather than before the visit.

items.h: Spares stock in the wrong place
items.p: A critical part sits in a warehouse eight hours away from the plant most likely to need it.
One group with four plants is handled as four unrelated customers, so nobody sees the whole relationship.

sections.h2: From the purchase department to the plant floor.

steps.p: Quotations to the purchase department from the catalogue, with the plant's technical contacts on the account.
Installation and commissioning jobs at the plant, closed with photo proof and the maintenance head signature.
The machine enters the asset register with its plant, line, serial number, warranty end and running hours basis.
An annual or comprehensive contract is recorded with its response commitment and the planned visit count.
Preventive schedules are raised by date or by running hours, and aligned to the plant's shutdown windows.
A breakdown call is logged, an engineer with the right skill is dispatched, and the job card is filled offline on the shop floor.
Response times, downtime, parts consumed and contract profitability are available per plant and per group.

items.q: Can assets be organised by plant and production line?
items.a: Yes. Each asset carries its customer, site and location detail, so a group with several plants can be navigated from the group down to a specific machine on a specific line, with its contract and service history attached.

items.q: Does maintenance scheduling support running hours rather than dates?
items.a: Yes. Preventive maintenance can be scheduled on a calendar basis or on meter and usage readings, which suits machines whose service interval depends on hours run rather than months elapsed.

items.q: Will the engineer app work inside a plant with no signal?
items.a: Yes. The mobile job card works offline: the engineer records the fault, parts fitted, photographs and the customer signature, and the job syncs when the device regains a connection.

items.q: Can one contract cover several plants of the same customer?
items.a: Yes. Multi-site contracts hold assets across a group's locations under one agreement, while each site keeps its own visit schedule and service history. See service contract management.

items.q: Is this only for medical equipment businesses?
items.a: No. The platform is built for any trade that sells, installs and services, and the same modules serve industrial, electrical and building products distributors. The medical work is simply where most of the shipped experience is.

items.q: Can we see whether a service contract is worth renewing?
items.a: Contract profitability compares what a contract invoiced against the visits and parts consumed under it, so a contract that costs more to honour than it earns is visible before you quote the renewal.
